heroCommands.comment: Install TensorFlow (GPU support on Ubuntu and Windows)

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: TensorFlow is Google's open-source platform for building, training and deploying machine learning models. It provides Python and C++ APIs plus a large ecosystem of tools and libraries.
sixtySeconds.problem: Building machine learning models from scratch means writing the maths for tensors, gradients and hardware acceleration yourself. TensorFlow provides those building blocks and runs them on CPUs and GPUs.
whoFor: Developers adding ML features to applications
Teams deploying models to production, mobile or the web
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want a mature framework with a big ecosystem for training and deploying models, especially if your team already uses it. Many newer research projects use PyTorch, so check what the models you need are written in.
requirements: Optional: a CUDA-enabled NVIDIA GPU on Ubuntu or Windows
Other devices (DirectX, macOS Metal) through device plugins

overview: TensorFlow was created by researchers and engineers on the Google Brain team for machine learning and neural network research, and is general enough for many other uses. It offers stable Python and C++ APIs, with other language bindings that are not guaranteed to stay backward compatible.

The standard pip package includes support for CUDA-enabled GPUs on Ubuntu and Windows, and a smaller CPU-only package is available. DirectX and macOS Metal devices are supported through device plugins, and Docker images and source builds are documented on tensorflow.org.
Nightly builds are published as tf-nightly for testing. The tensorflow.org tutorials are the main place to learn it, and release and security announcements go out on the announce mailing list.
